summary:
**Verdict.** The two rankings merge into 12 distinct hypotheses.
- **Confirmed (2):** the clock fix with a New York-time volatility season, and the unsigned barrier-touch target.
- **Weakened (10):** none is fully refuted. Two direction conditioners are close to refuted by data already in the repo: the vol-change conditioner and the reversal-intensity gate.
- **What I did:** no code was run and nothing was changed. I read LOG H5-H92, the review, the outlook, the T01/T04/T09 code and tables, the H40/H52 outputs and fwdtest/download.py, and checked 6 citations on the web. All paths below are under D:/nt/nt_tactical/runs/tactical/.

**Largest corrections**
1. **Term-structure evidence belongs to a different target.**
   - T01/H72 "target B" is 4-hour vol-of-vol, the log std of the next four hourly log-RVs (`vB` in tasks/T01_vol_forward/t01_lib.py). It is not a 4-hour vol change.
   - So the +0.011 (H72) and +0.041 (T01) both rankings cite do not support the term-structure item.
   - A vol change over H equals the log-RV level forecast minus a known regressor, and HAR level forecasts at these horizons were already tested: H57 (240 min: PASS, then FAIL after the recut, H73) and H74 (240/1440 min on 2017-07..2018-12, the "clean" Look A).
2. **The clock defect is real, but its effect is overstated.**
   - The code is as claimed: t04_lib.py:20-22 and volnet/volnet_lib.py:41 read file time. T09 converts hours to UTC, but its weekend flag stays in file time (analysis.py:212).
   - HAR+tod and S3 use 1-2 sin/cos harmonics with a free phase, which absorb the constant 4-5 h offset. What remains is the DST switch and about 54 pre-splice days in T01's training. Because file time = New York time +8 h (DST) or +10 h (standard), the switch moves UTC-locked events by 1 h and New York-locked events by 2 h.
   - T04-A's 365-day-training months show the calendar effect at only +0.002..+0.013. The 2017-18 failure is better explained by a regime change (the Kraken study dates a break to Nov 2021) and by 14-105-day early training than by the clock.
3. **The venue arm is already done, and the gate's mechanism fails on Binance.**
   - T09 Q9 already ran the Binance-trained arm: next-open AUC 0.5383±0.0101.
   - On Binance, monthly AUC does not track lag-1 autocorrelation, VR or Roll (detrended r +0.06 / +0.06 / -0.13). That contradicts the reversal-intensity gate.
4. **The vol-change conditioner was largely tested in H40.** H40 already tested vol-trend terciles (v60/v24) as minute-direction conditioners: none significant. That ratio is the main driver of the vol-change forecast (dA_hat).
5. **H52 does not count against shock reversal.**
   - H52's "large moves" conditioned on the future move, not on a past shock.
   - But Kitron & Wengrowicz (arXiv 2608.21888, which exists) put the 15-minute reversal's gross edge at about 1.3 bp, below cost.
6. **Rank 10's "archived zips" do not exist.** download.py reads each zip in memory and keeps columns 0-5. The trade count needs a re-download, verifiable against the logged sha256.
7. **Power is too low for several criteria.**
   - Three prospective months give a t-interval with 2 df, about 4.3 SE wide.
   - The weekend gap needs an observed gap of at least 0.03 at 6 months.
   - The macro calendar has only about 11 events in 3 months.
   - The first hours of 2026-10-01 were already read as labels (T01 loads to 2026-10-02 00:00).

**Literature**
- **Kraken study (US-hours variance share 50.6% vs 38.4%):** confirmed through CryptoSlate. It links mdpi.com/1911-8074/19/9/707; the MDPI page returned 403.
- **Kitron & Wengrowicz:** the paper exists, but its +0.011 AUC gap compares crypto with equities. Ranking 2 rank 7 cites it as a session gap.
- **Kim & Hansen 2607.09426:** exists. It finds quarter-hour bursts in volatility and volume, which a low-order New York-time harmonic basis cannot fit; add a quarter-hour term.
- **"Wen et al. 2022":** this is Wen, Bouri, Xu & Zhao, NAJEF 62:101733, on intraday momentum and reversal over 2013-2020. It does not show that macro sensitivity grew after 2020.
- **New York Fed SR1052:** finds BTC largely orthogonal to macro news, except core CPI surprises.

**Order after verification** (confidences are estimates):
1. Re-stamp helper plus a New York-time basis with a quarter-hour term. P(defect real) is high; P(prospective pass) about 0.4.
2. Unsigned barrier touch, about 0.45.
3. Measurement-aware HAR as a data diagnostic, judged against S3 rather than bare HAR, about 0.25.
4. Vol-change term structure, judged only on the beyond-HAR clause, about 0.25.
5. Venue stage 1: arm A plus the matched month 2025-06 (diagnostic).
6. Then the weekend gap (6 months, about 0.3), the macro calendar (needs the owner's ruling, about 0.2-0.3) and event-time reversal (about 0.1).
7. Drop the vol-change conditioner and the reversal-intensity gate. Condition-based abstention runs only if a condition passes.

**Sources**
- Kraken study coverage: https://cryptoslate.com/crypto-never-closes-but-bitcoin-ethereum-xrp-and-solana-now-move-on-wall-street-time/
- Kitron & Wengrowicz: https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.21888
- Kim & Hansen: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.09426
- New York Fed SR1052: https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/media/research/staff_reports/sr1052.pdf
- Liberty Street Economics: https://libertystreeteconomics.newyorkfed.org/2023/02/is-there-a-bitcoin-macro-disconnect/

checks.name: Clock-correct volatility seasonality and New York-time basis (R1#1, R2#1)
checks.reason: (1) Untested: confirmed. T04-A built its 96 slots from the raw timestamp (tasks/T04_vol_calendar/t04_lib.py:20-22), and volnet/volnet_lib.py:41 does the same. No study used a re-stamped clock or a New York basis. T04-B uses true-UTC Binance slots, so it is unaffected. (2) Literature: confirmed through CryptoSlate. It links mdpi.com/1911-8074/19/9/707 (the MDPI page returned 403) and gives 50.6% vs 38.4% of variance in 13-22 UTC, a peak at 14 UTC in DST and 15 UTC otherwise, US holidays 55.7% to 41.9%, and a break in Nov 2021. (3) Our data shows the consequence is overstated. HAR+tod and S3 use 1-2 free-phase sin/cos harmonics (volnet_lib.py:41; vol/volbench.py:21), which absorb the constant 4-5 h offset. What remains is the DST switch: 1 h for UTC-locked events and 2 h for New York-locked ones, because file time = New York +8 h or +10 h. T01's frozen fit has about 54 of 365 days before the splice. In T04-A's months with 365-day training, S3C - S3 is +0.002..+0.013 and C - ar is +0.006..+0.019 (tablesA.txt). That is far below +0.076, so 2017-18 most likely lacked the effect (regime). Kim & Hansen (2607.09426) report UTC-locked quarter-hour bursts in volatility, which harmonics of order 4 or less cannot fit: add a quarter-hour term, or the basis may lose to the 96 slots on criterion (b). (4) The protocol is honest, but it largely re-tests T04-B's effect on the same months. With 3 months the t-interval has 2 df and is about 0.055 wide, so use the 3/6-month Pocock looks. T01 already read the first hours of 2026-10-01 as labels; start scoring from 2026-10-02. Confidence: high that the defect exists; about 0.4 for a prospective pass.

checks.name: Vol-change term structure: 15 min, 4 h, 1 day (R1#2, R2#2)
checks.reason: (1) Only partly untested. The cited evidence is for another target: T01/H72 target B is vol-of-vol, vB = log std of the next four hourly log-RVs (t01_lib.build; gaps/study3_vov.py:24), not a 4-hour vol change. So H72's +0.011 and T01's +0.041 do not support it. The change over H is the log-RV level forecast minus a known regressor that is in S1. So beyond-HAR content at these horizons was already tested: H57 at 15/60/240 min (+0.006 Spearman, QLIKE fails; 240 min went from PASS to FAIL after the recut, H73), H71/H74 at 240/1440 min, and H72(2). (2) The literature is not at issue. (3) Our data shows small beyond-HAR gains. H83 found HAR levels alone at +0.115 over the weak AR, so the 'skill vs AR >= 0.02' clause passes trivially; only the beyond-HAR clause is informative. H91 notes the H53 rise (0.29 -> 0.40) may partly be a $1-tick staleness artefact. (4) Protocol: the recipe is frozen, which is honest. But Look A is not clean in substance: H74 used 2017-07..2018-12 as its confirmation block for 240/1440-min HAR forecasts, and T04 SPEC.md says so. P(4-hour passes prospectively) is about 0.25-0.3, not 0.5. The 15-minute target C is likely below the bar (H57, H72(2)).

checks.name: Unsigned fixed-size barrier-touch probability (R1#7, R2#3)
checks.reason: (1) Untested: confirmed. Earlier barrier work was signed (H33, H38, H48, H50; hourly/hourly.py first_touch). H69 scored excess beyond a HAR band, H54 the up/down asymmetry, and T03 terminal-return intervals. No study uses an unsigned fixed-bps touch target. (2) Broadie-Glasserman-Kou exists, but it corrects close-sampled paths. Labels from 1-minute high/low are close to continuously monitored, so applying that shift is a technical error. Drop it, or use closes. (3) Our data does not contradict it: H67 found the hour Brownian in its own clock to within about 0.01. But the decisive ingredient, HAR sigma against trailing-RV sigma on Binance 2025-11..2026-09, was already scored by T03: about 2.2-4.5% better interval score, 11/11 months. So the outcome there is largely predictable. Ranking 2's '0.448 forward' is H83's Spearman for the vol-change target, not for |r|. (4) The protocol is honest: arms are fixed on 2019..2024-06, X >= 25 bps keeps bounce wicks out, and the cutoff is respected. It is formally clean, but it measures largely T03's known HAR edge restated for a new target. P(Brier skill >= 2%) is about 0.45. It is useful to the owner, not a breakthrough.

checks.name: Measurement-aware HAR: HARQ, ranges, subsampled RV (R1#4, R2#5)
checks.reason: (1) Untested: confirmed. A grep finds no Parkinson, Garman-Klass, HARQ or subsampled run. H91 README open item 8 asks for exactly this. (2) Literature: Bollerslev-Patton-Quaedvlieg 2016 (J. Econometrics) exists, with gains at daily horizons on 5-minute RV (gathered.md:567). Realised quarticity from 15 one-minute returns is very noisy, so HARQ at 15 min may be unstable. (3) Our own data contradicts it. T01 shows S1 (log-RV + hour) transfers from Bitstamp to Binance with no loss: frozen +0.1295 vs refit +0.1271. The frozen-vs-refit gap (+0.142 vs +0.178) sits in S2/S3's volume and range extras. So Ranking 2's 'the gap points at input definitions' is wrong, and Ranking 1's criterion 'gap at most half of HAR-RV1's' is ill-posed, because HAR-RV1's gap is about 0. S3 already holds ranges (lrg15, lrg60) and half of H57's gain came from them. The incumbent should therefore be S3 or H57's extras, not bare HAR-RV1, or a pass only rediscovers H57. The '12% zero-volume minutes' held only from 2024-09-13 to 2025-03-15, then 0.6-0.8% (H91 README:88-89). The Binance Roll spread is about 0-2.5 bps, so expect little gain on the venue that judges. (4) Protocol: honest. Its real value is as a diagnostic of whether the 2022-10 HAR step is a staleness artefact. P(pass) is about 0.2-0.25.

checks.name: US macro-release calendar as a volatility regressor (R1#3)
checks.reason: (1) Untested: confirmed. No SPEC or REPORT uses FOMC/CPI/NFP; they appear only in the literature table of H91. (2) Literature is misattributed or contested. 'Wen et al. 2022' is Wen, Bouri, Xu & Zhao, NAJEF 62:101733, on intraday momentum and reversal over 2013-2020 with FOMC days as a condition. It cannot show that sensitivity grew after 2020. The New York Fed SR1052 finds BTC largely orthogonal to macro news except core CPI surprises. Supporting work: Ben Omrane et al. 2025 (5-minute data, US monetary news, larger in the pandemic) and Corbet et al. 2020 (JFS, FOMC). (3) The size estimate is overstated. FOMC, CPI, NFP and PCE give about 44 releases a year, not about 100. Their [-15,+60] windows cover about 0.6% of hours, not 2%, so +0.01..+0.03 overall skill is optimistic; +0.003..+0.01 is more plausible. (4) Protocol: honest and needs re-stamping first. But it is underpowered: about 11 events in 3 prospective months cannot meet '10% better in event windows with monthly CI > 0'. Only the 2024-07..2025-07-20 look (about 55 events) has some power. The D-050 owner ruling is correctly flagged. P about 0.2-0.3.

checks.name: Venue-matched direction: Bitstamp-trained vs Binance-trained (R1#9, R2#4)
checks.reason: (1) Partly tested. Arm B already exists: T09 Q9 trained only on Binance from 2025-10, up to 60 days, and gave next-open AUC 0.5383±0.0101 (run_forward.py docstring; tables.txt:1808-1814). Untested are arm A (the frozen Bitstamp tb7 scored per minute on Binance) and the matched month 2025-06 (D:/nt/nt_fwd_data/BTCUSDT_1m_2025-06.csv exists). (2) The literature is not at issue. (3) Data checks: R2's 'low volume worst, 0.5226 vs 0.5369 mid' comes from the CLOSE-entry table (tables.txt:1124-1130). At next open, the protocol's label, low 0.5243 equals high 0.5242. In 2017-19 at next open, low volume was also worst (0.5395), so 'the reverse of 2017-20' does not hold, and the hygiene arm A' has weak support. 2025-06 falls in Bitstamp's cleaned regime after 2025-03-15 (zero-volume minutes 0.6-0.8%), so the matched month tests only the late feed. T09 found the weights interchangeable. (4) Protocol: labelled exploratory, which is honest. B against A is confounded by training length (1-11 months vs 365 days; H56: longer training is better). A one-month matched test has an AUC SE of about 0.011 per feed, so detecting 0.01 is borderline. It is diagnostic value only; P(venue gap >= 0.01) is about 0.3.

checks.name: Event-time reversal after HAR-scaled shocks (R1#5, R2#6)
checks.reason: (1) Partly untested. Every T09 number cited checks out in tables.txt. Next open, move1bps q97-100, 2024-25: 0.5370±0.0281, bps_all 1.532, top 10% 5.311. move1sig q97-100 2024-25: -0.641 / +0.208. Binance q97-100: 0.6230±0.0670 over 7 months, 647 top trades, bps_all 2.677. By era, bps_all 2.10/2.60/1.53 and top 10% 6.5/7.7/5.3. H52 is not evidence against: its 'large moves' were conditioned on the FUTURE move (decay/report.log Q3), not a past shock, and both rankings misread it. But tb7 already holds sd-scaled returns over 1/5/10/15/20/30 bars, and 'rich' holds wick and volume-surge features (H27, H56). T09 Q7 also scored the stretched top decile on Binance (hit 0.557, +0.65 bps). So R2's claim that k = 5/15 is 'clean on Binance' is only partly true. (2) Kitron & Wengrowicz (2608.21888) exists and supports reversal after aggressive moves, but puts the gross edge at about 1.3 bp per trade, below 5 bp round trip. (3) This undercuts the '> 2 bps' route. (4) The protocol is honest, but at 6 months the event AUC SE is about 0.017-0.02, so the joint criterion needs an observed gap of about 0.04. P(pass) is 0.1 or less.

checks.name: Weekend and session conditional reversal (R1#6, R2#7)
checks.reason: (1) Weekend partly seen. T09 tables confirm weekend beats weekday in all 9 years at next open. But the 2017-19 gaps are +0.003..+0.007, not R2's +0.012..+0.030. The gap grew from 2020 (+0.015..+0.031) and was +0.011 in 2025. Pooled 2024-25: 0.5458±0.0142 vs 0.5220±0.0069. Binance: 0.5583±0.0195 vs 0.5328±0.0093, bps_all +0.48 / +0.72. T09's weekend flag is in file time before the splice (analysis.py:212), so a correct-clock weekend is new for 2017-24. H40's weekend cell was +0.006 n.s. (2) Kitron's +0.011 AUC gap compares crypto with equities, not sessions; R2 misapplies it. (3) The hour part is noise. In 2024-25 UTC, hours 14/17/18/19 are 0.507-0.516, but 22 UTC (0.513) is as low, and each cell's half-width is about 0.03. T09 REPORT: 'No hour-of-day structure.' H40's US session (file 16-24 = UTC 11/12-19/20) covered other years. (4) The protocol is honest but underpowered. On Binance the monthly SD of the gap is about 0.028, so at 6 months the SE is about 0.0115 and CI > 0 needs an observed gap >= 0.03. P is about 0.3, not 0.6-0.7. It stays below 2 bps.

checks.name: Vol-change forecast (dA_hat) as a direction conditioner (R1#8, R2#8)
checks.reason: (1) Largely tested. H40 pre-registered vol-trend terciles (v60/v24; regimes/SPEC.md:13) as minute-direction conditioners. Results: lo -0.009, mid +0.006, hi +0.002, none significant after Holm (regimes/part1.log). dA_hat's main driver is the same mean-reversion of short against long volatility. (2) Ranking 2 cites Nagel 2012, but Nagel finds reversal profits rise when volatility (VIX) is high. That contradicts 'falling expected vol means the fade works'. (3) Volatility level does not condition AUC: T09 next-open 2024-25 terciles 0.5290 / 0.5281 / 0.5286, Binance 0.538 / 0.539 / 0.533. H54 and H78/H79 are also negative. (4) The protocol is honest, and Binance is clean for this exact cut. Close to refuted. P is about 0.1.

checks.name: Binance kline trade count as a volatility regressor (R1#10)
checks.reason: (1) Untested: confirmed; a grep finds no kline trade count, and download.py keeps only columns 0-5. (2) Jones-Kaul-Lipson 1994 (RFS) and Ané-Geman 2000 (JF) exist and tie volatility to the number of trades; this is from my own knowledge, not checked online. (3) The data does not contradict it: Bitstamp volume is about 6% of Binance's, with 1-minute correlation 0.44 (fwdtest/AMENDMENT.md), and S3's volume extras help. But T01 shows exactly those volume and range extras transfer worst between feeds. (4) Factual error in the protocol: there are no archived zips. download.py reads each zip in memory (io.BytesIO) and saves only the sha256 to download_log.json, so re-extraction means a re-download, verifiable against those hashes. It can be judged prospectively only, and needs the owner's ruling on D-050. P(+0.01 over S3) is about 0.25.

checks.name: Gate on trailing reversal intensity: AC1, VR, Roll (R2#9)
checks.reason: (1) Untested at the 1-7 day scale: confirmed; H68 and H76 differ. (2) The literature is not at issue. (3) Our data contradicts it on the venue that would judge it. T09 Q9 on Binance: the detrended correlation of monthly AUC with AC1 is +0.060 (p 0.86), with VR(1,15) +0.059 and with Roll -0.126 (tables.txt:1970-1978). Binance AC1 sits between -0.05 and +0.02, so the gate variable barely varies. The Bitstamp -0.51 is contemporaneous, within the same month, and partly mechanical. The VR standard errors given (0.11 for 1 day, 0.04 for 7 days) are correct. (4) The protocol is honest. Close to refuted. P is about 0.1.

checks.name: Abstention by exogenous condition with risk-coverage curves (R2#10)
checks.reason: It is contingent on items 6-9, and those are weakened or close to refuted. H90 shows |score| ordering stopped sorting trades forward (top decile hit 0.48), and condition cells on Binance are wide (weekend ±0.0195; q97-100 is 7 months, ±0.067). Per-cell (Mondrian) calibration on monthly cells this noisy will be unstable. The protocol is honest: a prospective freeze if any condition was seen. Run it only if a condition passes. P is about 0.1.

checks.name: Cross-check: cited literature
checks.reason: Kraken study: exists per CryptoSlate (it links mdpi.com/1911-8074/19/9/707, consistent with JRFM 19(9):707; the primary page returned 403), and the numbers match the claims. Kitron & Wengrowicz, arXiv 2608.21888 (submitted 2026-08-22): exists. Its +0.011 [+0.008,+0.014] AUC gap is crypto against US equities, and its gross edge is about 1.3 bp, below a 5 bp round trip. Ranking 2 rank 7 cites the gap as session evidence. Kim & Hansen, arXiv 2607.09426: exists. It finds quarter-hour bursts in volatility and volume on Binance perpetuals, which bears on rank 1's basis. 'Wen et al. 2022' is misattributed: it is NAJEF 62:101733 on intraday momentum and reversal over 2013-2020. HARQ (BPQ 2016), Broadie-Glasserman-Kou 1997, Nagel 2012, Jones-Kaul-Lipson 1994 and Ané-Geman 2000 are real papers, from my own knowledge. Nagel's sign contradicts ranking 2 rank 8's mechanism.

checks.name: Cross-check: protocol honesty and power
checks.reason: Cutoffs are respected: the main file is read only to 2025-07-20, 2025-07-21..2025-09-30 is never read, and selection uses only past spans. One overstatement: '2026-10-01..10-12 stay unread' is not strictly true. T01 loads to 2026-10-02 00:00 for the labels of late-September anchors (t01_lib.py:19), and T02 to 2026-10-01 00:00. So start prospective scoring at 2026-10-02 or declare it. About 8 new prospective freezes would share 2026-10..12 with T04-B and T05-B, so Holm over the family plus 2-df t-intervals (about 4.3 SE wide) make 3-month verdicts weak. Pre-register 6-month looks (Pocock) for everything except the hourly volatility targets. Several looks called clean are partly seen: Look A for 4-hour and 1-day volatility (H74), and the Binance stretched tail (T09 Q7). The T03 note in the barrier-touch check is about predictability only, not a breach.
